meta.homeTitle: Star Wars Semantic Atlas: why embeddings call two characters similar
meta.homeDescription: Explore 15 Star Wars character descriptions in embedding space. See the 2D maps, similarity graph, and cosine matrix, check them against the article's claims, and download the evidence.
meta.exploreDescription: Select a character to see its five nearest neighbors by cosine similarity, with PCA/UMAP maps, a threshold graph, and a matrix. Every score comes from the shipped bundle.
meta.methodologyDescription: Inputs, model revision, cosine and projection settings, article claim checks, limitations, and reproduction steps for the Star Wars Semantic Atlas.

footer.built: Offline embeddings prepared ahead of time; no model or provider calls in your browser.
footer.article: Based on the article “Mapping the Star Wars Universe”
footer.fanNote: An unofficial fan and education project. Star Wars names belong to their owners. No images are used.

home.title: Why does a model think two Star Wars characters are alike?
home.lead: Fifteen short character descriptions from one blog article, embedded with an open sentence model. Pick a character and look at its nearest neighbors, the scores behind them, and the words that produced them.
home.previewCaption: PCA projection of the authored descriptions, drawn from bundle {version}. Positions are 2D approximations. Rankings use the original {dims}-dimensional cosine scores.
home.previewLabel: Scatter plot of 15 characters in the PCA projection. {selected} is highlighted.

cards.neighborsBody: Every ranking uses cosine similarity on the original normalized vectors, never distances on the 2D map.
cards.variantBody: Switch to a variant with the named relationship phrases removed, then compare the text diff and the recomputed neighbors.
cards.evidenceBody: Every cluster claim in the article is turned into a test on the shipped scores, with the numbers shown next to it.

explore.heading: Explore the atlas
explore.intro: Pick a character from the list or the chart. Hovering previews a character; clicking or pressing Enter selects it. Every score comes from bundle {version}.

chart.legendShape: Marker shape and color show the editorial Force status. This is a label, not an embedding axis.
chart.legendNeighbors: Numbered markers are the selected character's nearest neighbors in the original space. Map distance can disagree with them.

chart.emptyVisible: Every character is hidden by the filters. Clear a filter to see the chart.

graph.noEdges: No pair meets this threshold. That is a valid result, not an error.
graph.curatedLegend: Dashed arrows are curated story relationships (editorial, directed, no similarity score).
graph.similarityLegend: Solid lines are cosine similarity edges (undirected). Thicker means higher.

methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.lead: What goes in, what is computed, what can be reproduced, and where the numbers stop being evidence.

inputs.heading: Inputs
inputs.body: The 15 descriptions are quoted verbatim from the “{section}” code block of the article “{title}” (lines {start}–{end}). They are unedited, so no description version has been recorded yet. They were written to encode faction, role, Force sensitivity, era, and relationships, so similarity reflects those word choices.

model.heading: Embedding model
model.body: Each description is encoded separately (batch size 1, CPU, one thread) with {model} at an exact pinned revision. Vectors are L2-normalized, checked for unit norm within 1e-5, and zero vectors are rejected. The model ran once, offline, when the bundle was prepared. Your browser only reads the saved results.

computation.heading: Similarity, neighbors, and graph
computation.cosine: Scores are cosine similarity between the original normalized {dims}-dimensional vectors. An independent NumPy recomputation matches the exported matrix within 1e-6. The matrix is symmetric and its diagonal is 1.
computation.neighbors: The neighbor list excludes the character itself, sorts by descending score, and breaks ties by id. Filters change which characters are eligible, not the scores.
computation.graph: Similarity edges are undirected and include each unordered pair once when cosine ≥ threshold. The default threshold is {threshold}. Scores from this model sit in a narrow band ({min} to {max}), so small threshold steps change the graph a lot. At threshold 1 the graph keeps any pair that truly scores 1, which here is none. Curated story edges are drawn separately and never carry a score.

projections.heading: Projections
projections.body: PCA (full SVD, deterministic sign) and UMAP (n_neighbors 5, min_dist 0.3, cosine metric, seeds 7, 21, and 42, single-threaded) were fitted once and exported. The browser never refits them. A seed alone does not guarantee identical UMAP output, so the package versions and execution settings are recorded below.

editorial.heading: Editorial layer (draft)
editorial.body: Allegiance, role, era, Force status, the classification notes, the 21 curated story relationships, and the relationship-free variants were drafted from the descriptions' own wording. They are marked draft, are not canon, and are not embedding axes. The article's plotting code now follows the descriptions; where an earlier version disagreed (Ahsoka, Kylo Ren, Leia, Boba Fett), the note records it, and Ahsoka's allegiance is marked disputed. The map's faction colors come from this layer: Jedi Order, Sith, Rebellion, bounty hunters, and gray for unknown or disputed.

variant.heading: Description variant
variant.body: The variant removes named relationship phrases such as “son of Anakin Skywalker” or “trained by Yoda”. It keeps identity aliases such as “formerly Ben Solo”. Each variant has its own input hash, vectors, matrix, and projections. Several phrases change at once, so a shift in neighbors does not isolate one cause.

claims.heading: Article claims, retested
claims.body: Each narrative claim in the article is turned into a concrete test on the shipped scores. Where a claim concerns the 2D picture, it is tested in the original space, and the test text says so.

reproduce.heading: Reproduce
reproduce.body: From the project root, one command rebuilds the bundle. It downloads the pinned model revision on the first run, writes content-hashed files and a manifest, and fails if any check does not pass. Rebuilding in the same environment reproduces the same hashes. Identical floating-point output on other hardware is not guaranteed.

downloads.heading: Downloads
downloads.body: The zip holds the descriptions, normalized embeddings, original-space cosine matrices, projection parameters and coordinates, claim checks, the manifest, and a README. CSV cells are protected against spreadsheet formulas.

version.heading: Bundle version
version.body: Version {version}, schema v{schema}, created {created}. Measured output from the offline pipeline. Editorial fields are hand-authored drafts. Compressed bundle size: {size}.
